speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The crying gets worse when you touch his belly? That is a very important clue. To better understand what might be happening inside, have you noticed any changes in his stool, such as it being bloody or very foul-smelling?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever, vomiting, or diarrhea, and a normal birth history make infectious causes less likely. Since the abdominal pain is significant and the baby is refusing feeds, I need to check for blood in the stool and rule out a surgical emergency like intussusception. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Occult_Blood. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have ordered the necessary stool test and abdominal ultrasound to evaluate for intussusception and other surgical causes; while your note mentions lower abdominal discomfort, the lack of fever or vomiting and normal birth history point toward a non-infectious etiology. Please ensure the ultrasound images and stool results are returned immediately so I can finalize the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception
